column1: # reviewer-sources.tsv — the single reviewer-source registry (issue #1425).
# One row per third-party review bot (GitHub App) the org recognizes. This is the
# source of truth that three consumers agree with, so their lists can never drift:
#   * dev-lead's trust check   — scripts/dev-lead-intent.sh (TRUSTED_BOTS)
#   * the advisory approval gate — scripts/lib/advisory-review-gate.sh (ADVISORY_BOTS,
#                                  RATE_LIMIT_NOTICE_BOTS)
#   * the reviewer scorecard    — scripts/reviewer_report.sh (REVIEWER_BOTS)
# Read by scripts/lib/reviewer-sources.sh. Data, not code — register a reviewer by
# adding a row; tests/test_reviewer_sources.bats asserts the three consumer lists
# stay projections of this file and enforces the invariant below.
# THE #1425 INVARIANT — (can create a review thread) ⇒ (dev-lead may act on it):
#   any row with creates_threads=yes MUST have dev_lead_trusted=yes. A bot that
#   posts inline review comments creates a review thread, and an unresolved thread
#   trips required_review_thread_resolution and blocks the merge; if dev-lead is not
#   permitted to act on it, no automation can clear it (the 2026-08-02 deadlock,
#   root-caused to graphite-app). A source that only posts a top-level comment
#   (creates_threads=no) MAY be advisory-only-and-non-blocking (dev_lead_trusted=no)
#   with the reason recorded in the rationale column.
# schema_version: 1
# Columns (tab-separated):
#   login            — the bot's GraphQL App login (no "[bot]" suffix). dev-lead's
#                      webhook-facing trusted set appends "[bot]" to each login.
#   creates_threads  — yes|no: posts inline review comments (→ blocking review thread).
#   dev_lead_trusted — yes|no: in dev-lead's trusted set (dev-lead may act on it).
#   advisory_gate    — yes|no: one of the bots the advisory approval gate waits on.
#   rationale        — why this bot is classified as it is.
